payload.title: [native-swift-3] Malformed inbound frame with a NaN/Inf float crashes the client (Int(Double) trap) — remote DoS
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-swift-3 (medium/dos, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: packages/swift/Sources/FrickSwift/FrickSyncSocket.swift
LINES: 162-169, 527, 1469-1485

WHAT: `FrickMsgPackValue.intValue` converts a decoded `.double` via `Int(v)` with no finiteness guard (line 166). `Int(Double.nan)`/`Int(.infinity)` is a fatal runtime trap (verified). The decoder produces `.double` for msgpack float32/float64 (0xCA/0xCB, lines 431-436) for ANY bit pattern including NaN/Inf. `decodeFrame` calls `parts[0].intValue` to read the frame kind (line 527), so a single inbound frame encoded as `[<NaN float>, payload]` crashes the receive loop / process. This is pre-existing for `decodeFrame`, but the new FR-144 `decodeObjectRemoval` adds another reachable trap site: `tuple[0].intValue` on a server-controlled `removed` tuple (line 1473).

IMPACT: A malicious or buggy server (or a MITM on a non-TLS local transport) can hard-crash the Swift client with one crafted frame. Denial of service; no recovery since it traps rather than throws.

SUGGESTED FIX: Guard the double→Int conversion: `case .double(let v): return v.isFinite ? Int(exactly: v.rounded()) : nil` (and use `Int(exactly:)` to reject out-of-range). Apply everywhere `intValue` feeds array allocation / required fields.
